best_architecture: Use the high-level McpServer class (from @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js) rather than the low-level Server + setRequestHandler API. McpServer wraps the protocol layer and handles capability negotiation, request routing, and automatic Zod-to-JSON-Schema conversion + runtime input validation. The recommended pattern is a modular, domain-driven, layered architecture that separates three concerns: (1) protocol/transport wiring, (2) tool business logic, and (3) shared services/state. Concretely, structure the project as src/index.ts (entry point + server bootstrap + transport selection + graceful shutdown), src/tools/ (one file per domain, each exporting a registration function), src/schemas/ (Zod schemas, one per tool), src/services/ (shared API clients, IPC to the Python orchestrator, retry/timeout logic), src/types.ts (z.infer-derived types), and src/constants.ts. For 20+ tools, the critical decision is to NOT register every tool inline in index.ts: instead give each tool module a registerXxxTools(server) function and call them from a central registry, OR adopt directory-based auto-discovery (as mcp-framework does). Each tool is registered via server.registerTool(name, {title, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, annotations}, handler). Key design decisions that matter most: (1) STDIO HYGIENE -- stdout is reserved exclusively for JSON-RPC messages; ALL logging MUST go to stderr (console.error or a stderr-bound logger). A single stray console.log to stdout corrupts the JSON-RPC stream and breaks the client. This is the #1 architectural constraint for a stdio server. (2) NEVER throw from a tool handler -- catch all errors and return a CallToolResult with isError:true and a text content block; an uncaught throw can crash the server or produce a protocol-level error rather than a tool-level error the LLM can recover from. (3) Use Zod with .strict() and .describe() on every field so unknown keys are rejected and the LLM gets rich JSON Schema descriptions. (4) Provide structuredContent (machine-readable) alongside content[].text (human/LLM-readable) when an outputSchema is declared. (5) For large outputs, enforce a CHARACTER_LIMIT (~25k chars) and truncate with a helpful message + pagination (offset/limit, has_more, next_offset) so a single tool call cannot blow the context window. (6) Graceful shutdown: register SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers that call transport.close()/server.close() and flush state before process.exit. (7) Tool naming: snake_case, service/domain-prefixed (e.g. fs_read_file, git_commit) to avoid collisions across 20+ tools. Streaming over stdio: the stdio transport itself does not stream partial tool results within a single tool call (a CallToolResult is returned whole); for incremental progress use the MCP progress-notification mechanism (notifications/progress via a progressToken) and/or log to stderr -- true chunked streaming is a feature of the Streamable HTTP transport, not stdio. For Local-Claw (Python orchestrator <-> TS server over stdin/stdout) stdio is the correct transport: it is the simplest, most secure (no network surface, OS process isolation), and lowest-latency option. Enable TypeScript strict mode, target ES2022, use ESM ("type": "module", module/moduleResolution Node16+), and prefer unknown over any.

pitfalls: STDOUT POLLUTION (the #1 stdio killer): any console.log(), process.stdout.write(), or library that writes JSON/text to stdout corrupts the JSON-RPC stream. The client's framing parser chokes on the non-JSON-RPC bytes interleaved with real messages. This is SILENT DATA CORRUPTION, not a crash -- the server keeps running, tool calls intermittently fail or hang, and there is no error message. Gemma's spec must mandate: stdout is JSON-RPC ONLY; ALL logging (and any third-party lib output, e.g. dotenv banner, ORM query logs) goes to stderr. Audit every dependency for stdout writes at startup.

THROWING FROM A TOOL HANDLER: an uncaught throw inside a handler bubbles up as a PROTOCOL-LEVEL JSON-RPC error, not a tool-level result. The agent (Python Brain) receives a hard error it cannot reason about or recover from -- it cannot see the error text in a normal CallToolResult and the conversation loop can crash. CORRECT pattern: wrap every handler body in try/catch and return { content: [{ type: 'text', text: errorMessage }], isError: true }. The LLM can then read the error and retry or adapt.

ZOD SCHEMA WITHOUT .strict(): a plain z.object() silently STRIPS unknown keys by default and (worse, with .passthrough()) lets unexpected keys flow through. Without .strict() the LLM can send malformed/hallucinated arguments that pass validation, producing confusing behavior. Use z.object({...}).strict() so unknown fields are REJECTED with a clear validation error the handler can surface as isError.

MISSING .describe() ON ZOD FIELDS: the SDK converts the Zod schema to the JSON Schema sent in tools/list. Fields without .describe() produce a schema with no field documentation, so the LLM must guess each argument's meaning -- directly degrading tool-use accuracy. Every field AND the tool itself must carry a description.

EXTERNAL $ref IN JSON SCHEMA: MCP requires self-contained inputSchema/outputSchema. A schema with external $ref (e.g. pointing at a remote URL or a shared $defs file the client can't resolve) breaks client-side parsing/validation. Keep schemas inline; if Zod emits $ref/$defs for reused sub-schemas, inline them or ensure $defs are bundled within the same schema document.

NO OUTPUT TRUNCATION: returning a 50k-100k+ character tool result (e.g. a full file dump, git log, or directory tree) silently blows the agent's context window -- it is a quality killer, not an error. Enforce a CHARACTER_LIMIT (~25k) and truncate with an explanatory suffix + pagination metadata (offset/limit/has_more/next_offset) so the agent can page through large results deterministically.

MISSING SIGTERM HANDLER: containers (RunPod, k8s) send SIGTERM on scale-down/redeploy. With no handler the process is killed mid-flight: in-flight tool calls are lost, no graceful drain, the Python client sees a broken pipe. Register BOTH SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers that stop accepting new work, await/flush in-flight calls, call transport.close()/server.close(), then process.exit(0).

MONOLITHIC index.ts: registering all 20+ tools inline in the entry file makes it thousands of lines, impossible to hot-reload per-domain, and merge-conflict-prone. Split into src/tools/<domain>.ts each exporting registerXxxTools(server), wired by a central registry (or directory auto-discovery). Keeps index.ts to bootstrap + transport + shutdown only.

BLOCKING THE EVENT LOOP IN A HANDLER: synchronous file I/O (fs.readFileSync), synchronous child_process (execSync), or CPU-bound work (large JSON.parse, hashing, regex on huge strings) inside a handler blocks the SINGLE Node event loop, stalling ALL concurrent MCP requests and progress notifications. Use async APIs (fs.promises, exec/spawn with await), and offload CPU-heavy work to a worker_thread or a child-process skill server.

ASSUMING TRUE STREAMING OVER STDIO: a single stdio tool call returns one whole CallToolResult -- you cannot stream partial chunks back inside it. Teams expecting token-by-token streaming over stdio get a long silent wait. Use notifications/progress (progressToken) for incremental status, or switch to Streamable HTTP if real intra-call streaming is required.

NOT PINNING THE SDK / SPEC VERSION: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and the spec move fast (breaking changes between minor versions; spec dated 2025-11-25 with more coming). Floating ^1.x can pull a release that changes registerTool signatures or schema handling. Pin an exact version and test before bumping.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: TypeScript MCP stdio server
  As the Local-Claw Python orchestrator (Brain)
  I want a robust TypeScript MCP server over stdio
  So that tool calls are discoverable, isolated, hygienic, and bounded

  Background:
    Given an McpServer is bootstrapped with StdioServerTransport
    And all domain tool modules have been registered via registerAllTools(server)

  Scenario: Tool discovery returns valid self-contained schemas
    Given the MCP server has started and completed the initialize handshake
    When the client sends a tools/list request
    Then the response includes every registered tool
    And each tool has a name, a description, and an inputSchema that is valid JSON Schema
    And no inputSchema contains an external $ref
    And every input field carries a description string

  Scenario: stdout hygiene is preserved under logging
    Given a tool handler that logs diagnostics during execution
    When the handler emits log output
    Then the log bytes are written to stderr only
    And stdout contains exclusively well-formed JSON-RPC messages
    And the client's JSON-RPC parser never encounters a framing error

  Scenario: Errors are isolated as tool-level results, not protocol errors
    Given a tool handler that throws an exception during execution
    When the tool is invoked via tools/call
    Then the handler's try/catch converts the throw into a CallToolResult
    And the result has isError set to true
    And the result content includes a text block with the error message
    And the client receives a normal tools/call response (not a JSON-RPC protocol error)

  Scenario: Large output is truncated and paginated
    Given a tool that would naturally return 100000 characters
    When the tool is invoked
    Then the returned content text is truncated at the CHARACTER_LIMIT (~25000)
    And the result includes a truncation notice
    And the structured metadata sets has_more to true with a next_offset
    And re-invoking the tool with that offset returns the following page

  Scenario: Graceful shutdown on container SIGTERM
    Given the server has an in-flight tool call executing
    When the process receives SIGTERM
    Then the server stops accepting new requests
    And the in-flight call is allowed to complete or is flushed
    And transport.close() and server.close() are invoked
    And the process exits with code 0 with no lost JSON-RPC responses
sota_improvements: STREAMABLE HTTP TRANSPORT (spec 2025-03-26, SDK 1.10.0+): the modern remote transport -- single /mcp endpoint handling POST/GET/DELETE, with server-to-client SSE for TRUE streaming within a single tool call (impossible over stdio). Stateful or stateless modes, optional resumability via an EventStore + priming events. Keep stdio for Local-Claw's local Brain<->server link, but expose remote skills over StreamableHTTPServerTransport. It is now the cross-host baseline (Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Goose) and the foundation for the experimental Tasks primitive.

TASKS PRIMITIVE (experimental, Nov 2025 spec, requires Streamable HTTP): a long-running tool invocation returns a HANDLE instead of a result; the client polls for completion. Ideal for slow skills (builds, large repo scans) so a tool call never blocks or times out -- supersedes ad-hoc job-id polling.

MCP PROXY / GATEWAY LAYER: put mcp-proxy (or nginx) in front of multiple skill MCP servers for routing, load balancing, and aggregation at scale -- the Brain talks to one endpoint while N child servers (TS/Rust/Python) sit behind it. Enables independent scaling and centralized auth/observability for the 20+ tool fleet.

AUTO-DISCOVERY VIA DIRECTORY SCAN (mcp-framework pattern): scan src/tools/*.ts at startup and auto-register exported tools instead of hand-maintaining registerXxxTools calls -- removes a whole class of 'forgot to wire the tool' bugs and supports per-file hot-reload during development.

TOOL ANNOTATIONS (readOnlyHint / destructiveHint / idempotentHint / openWorldHint): declare behavioral metadata per tool so the agent makes safer selection/retry decisions (e.g. retry idempotent reads freely, confirm destructive writes). Cheap to add, materially improves agent safety.

MCP RESOURCE SUBSCRIPTIONS (resources/subscribe + notifications/resources/updated): push file/state changes to the client instead of polling a status tool -- lower latency and fewer wasted tool calls for watching logs, file changes, or job state.

STRUCTURED OUTPUT (outputSchema + structuredContent, spec 2025-06-18): declare a Zod outputSchema and return typed structuredContent alongside content[].text so the Python Brain consumes machine-readable results instead of regexing text -- pairs naturally with the pagination metadata.

TYPESCRIPT 5.8 IMPORT ATTRIBUTES + NATIVE ESM RESOLUTION: with Node 22+'s native ESM handling and TS 5.8 import attributes, ship compiled ESM (or run Node's native loaders) and drop the tsx/ts-node transpile step in production for faster, lower-overhead startup -- keep tsx for dev watch only.
